waves.finding: A five-component regimen containing ivermectin, doxycycline, zinc, vitamin C, and vitamin D, with or without famotidine, was reported as generally well tolerated; the study was not designed to isolate the supplements' efficacy.
waves.safety: Multi-drug/multi-supplement design prevents attribution to vitamin C, vitamin D, or zinc and cannot support component-specific treatment claims.

waves.title: Ginseng as promising natural medicine against infectious diseases: Therapeutic targets and potential mechanisms.
waves.population: mixed experimental and limited clinical anti-infective literature
waves.finding: Ginsenosides show antiviral, antibacterial, immunomodulatory, and anti-inflammatory activity across experimental systems, but the evidence base is dominated by mechanistic and preclinical work.
waves.safety: Broad anti-infective mechanisms do not establish that ginseng treats human infections; pathogen-, extract-, and formulation-specific trials are needed.

waves.title: Combating saffron fraud: a systematic review of adulteration practices, detection technologies, recommendations and challenges.
waves.population: commercial saffron products and detection studies
waves.finding: The review found substantial geographic variability in saffron adulteration and documented substitution, dilution, and use of synthetic dyes including potentially hazardous colorants.
waves.safety: This is product-authenticity and consumer-safety evidence, not clinical efficacy evidence; prevalence estimates vary markedly by market and sampling method.

waves.title: Effectiveness of Whey Protein Supplementation in Weight Loss Interventions for Patients with Obesity: A Systematic Review.
waves.population: adults with obesity undergoing weight-loss interventions
waves.finding: Whey protein may help preserve fat-free mass during weight loss, especially when paired with resistance exercise or anabolic-enriched formulations, but many trials were neutral and certainty was frequently downgraded.
waves.safety: Whey effects are entangled with calorie restriction, exercise, leucine/vitamin-D enrichment, and varied interventions.

waves.title: Omega-3 fatty acid supplementation for distal symmetrical peripheral neuropathy in adults with diabetes mellitus.
waves.study: Cochrane systematic review of randomized trials
waves.population: adults with diabetes and distal symmetrical polyneuropathy
waves.finding: Evidence was inadequate to show meaningful improvement in peripheral-nerve impairment, neuropathy symptoms, pain, or quality of life; available adverse-event data did not show a clear harm signal but were very uncertain.
waves.safety: Direct clinical null/uncertain evidence should override mechanistic rationale for treating diabetic neuropathy with omega-3.

waves.title: Whey Protein Supplementation Combined with Exercise on Muscle Protein Synthesis and the AKT/mTOR Pathway in Healthy Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: healthy adults undergoing exercise protocols
waves.finding: Whey protein combined with exercise increased myofibrillar fractional synthetic rate and activated AKT/mTOR-related signaling after exercise.
waves.safety: This is an exercise-plus-protein interaction with short-term mechanistic endpoints; dose/timing meta-analysis should not be converted into a universal intake prescription.

waves.title: Efficacy of Alpha Lipoic Acid Supplementation in Sperm Parameters: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
waves.population: 250 men with infertility
waves.finding: Alpha-lipoic acid improved sperm morphology and motility measures over about three months but did not significantly improve pooled pregnancy rate, sperm concentration, live-sperm percentage, or total antioxidant capacity.
waves.safety: Surrogate semen improvements do not establish fertility or live-birth benefit; the trial base was small.

waves.title: Probiotics for the treatment of vulvovaginal candidiasis in nonpregnant women: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.population: nonpregnant women with vulvovaginal or recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis
waves.finding: Probiotics added to antifungals modestly improved some short-term cure outcomes and reduced six-month recurrence in low-certainty analyses, while probiotics alone were generally less effective than antifungals for sustained cure.
waves.safety: Evidence was low or very low certainty and strain/regimen dependent; probiotics should be framed as possible adjuncts rather than antifungal replacements.

waves.title: Synbiotic supplementation reduces intestinal permeability and inflammation in overweight or obese kidney transplant recipients: a randomized controlled trial.
waves.population: 46 overweight/obese kidney-transplant recipients
waves.finding: Twelve weeks of synbiotics reduced LBP, hs-CRP, IL-6, and sICAM-1 but did not significantly change creatinine, urea, MDA, or galectin-3.
waves.safety: Small transplant-population biomarker trial; inflammatory/permeability changes do not establish graft or cardiovascular outcome benefit.

waves.title: Clinical Assessment of the Effect of Hypericum perforatum Chewing Gum on Salivary Streptococcus mutans Count, pH, Plaque Index, and Gingival Bleeding: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
waves.population: 54 adults using extract-containing or control chewing gum
waves.finding: Hypericum-containing gum reduced Streptococcus mutans count, plaque index, and gingival bleeding more than control gum, while between-group salivary-pH differences were not significant.
waves.safety: Local chewing-gum formulation is not evidence for systemic oral St John's wort supplementation and has different interaction implications.

waves.title: Curcumin for the clinical treatment of rheumatoid arthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of placebo-controlled randomized clinical trials.
waves.population: 244 people with rheumatoid arthritis
waves.finding: Curcumin improved pooled disease-activity, inflammatory, pain, and joint-count outcomes, but certainty was very low for most endpoints and low for rheumatoid factor.
waves.safety: Large standardized effects from a small heterogeneous evidence base should be interpreted cautiously pending larger multicenter trials.

waves.title: Randomized, open-label study of the short-term pharmacokinetics of oral magnesium oxide in healthy volunteers.
waves.population: 24 healthy adult men
waves.finding: Single 750-mg and 2,000-mg magnesium-oxide doses produced non-dose-proportional serum magnesium exposure; the higher dose did not proportionally increase Cmax or AUC.
waves.safety: Both single doses were well tolerated in this small short-term study; these PK findings do not establish chronic-dose safety or efficacy.

waves.title: Astaxanthin and Male Reproductive Health: Mechanisms, Experimental Evidence, and Clinical Perspectives.
waves.population: preclinical and limited heterogeneous clinical male-fertility evidence
waves.finding: Astaxanthin has plausible antioxidant and mitochondrial mechanisms and some studies report semen-parameter improvements, but clinical findings remain limited and inconsistent.
waves.safety: Preclinical evidence dominates; large standardized RCTs with clinical reproductive outcomes are still required.

waves.title: Calcium, vitamin D, or combined supplementation to prevent fractures and falls: systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: 153,902 adults not receiving osteoporosis drug therapy
waves.finding: Calcium alone, vitamin D alone, and combined supplementation produced little to no clinically meaningful reduction in fractures or falls; evidence was mostly moderate to high certainty.
waves.safety: Strong direct null evidence for routine fracture/fall prevention in broadly community-dwelling adults; evidence was more limited in high-risk/residential populations.

waves.title: Vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy and offspring bone microarchitecture: A post hoc analysis of the MAVIDOS randomised controlled trial.
waves.study: post hoc analysis of a randomized placebo-controlled trial
waves.population: 222 children aged 6-7 born to women randomized to prenatal vitamin D or placebo
waves.finding: Prenatal cholecalciferol did not significantly alter offspring tibial cortical/trabecular microarchitecture or volumetric bone mineral density at age 6-7.
waves.safety: Post hoc subgroup of an established pregnancy RCT; null microarchitecture finding should remain separate from other reported offspring BMD outcomes.

waves.title: Cetoleic acid and other long-chain unsaturated fatty acids as neuroprotective nutraceuticals.
waves.population: cell, animal, metabolic, and indirect lipid evidence
waves.finding: Cetoleic and related long-chain monounsaturated fatty acids have plausible neuroprotective mechanisms, but direct evidence for cetoleic acid is sparse and largely preclinical.
waves.safety: No established human neuroprotective efficacy; mechanistic influence on EPA/DHA availability is not equivalent to clinical benefit.

waves.title: Effect of vitamin C and hesperidin on serum uric acid concentrations in healthy adults with high uric acid levels: the randomized controlled 'HesperidrinC trial'.
waves.population: 40 adults with elevated serum uric acid
waves.finding: Vitamin-C-containing drinks reduced serum uric acid without changing urinary uric-acid excretion or clearance; hesperidin alone did not drive the effect.
waves.safety: Short two-week biomarker trial in people with elevated uric acid; it does not establish gout prevention or long-term clinical benefit.

waves.title: Exploring the Therapeutic Potential of Panax Ginseng: A Comprehensive Review of Its Pharmacological Applications.
waves.population: mixed preclinical and clinical literature
waves.finding: The review summarizes wide-ranging proposed cognitive, immune, hepatic, bone, and lipid effects of Panax ginseng but does not provide a focused quantitative clinical synthesis for any single indication.
waves.safety: Useful background context only; broad pharmacology should not be promoted as condition-specific efficacy.

waves.title: The effect of melatonin on sleep quality and daytime sleepiness in Parkinson's disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials.
waves.population: 206 patients with Parkinson disease
waves.finding: Melatonin modestly improved sleep quality/daytime sleepiness overall, with positive subgroup estimates for short-term and immediate-release regimens, while lower-dose, longer-duration, and prolonged-release subgroups were not consistently significant.
waves.safety: Small subgroup counts make dose/formulation comparisons exploratory; no dosing rule should be inferred.

waves.title: The efficacy of saffron supplementation on inflammation and oxidative stress in patients with type-2 diabetes mellitus: a meta-analysis.
waves.population: 261 people with type 2 diabetes
waves.finding: Saffron reduced TNF-alpha but did not significantly change CRP, IL-6, IL-10, MDA, or total antioxidant capacity.
waves.safety: Small evidence base and mostly null inflammatory/oxidative outcomes argue against broad anti-inflammatory claims in T2D.

waves.title: L-Carnitine in Dermatology: A Systematic Review of Therapeutic Potential and Biomarker Applications.
waves.population: mixed topical/systemic dermatology studies and biomarker literature
waves.finding: Topical and systemic L-carnitine showed signals across acne, sebum, hyperpigmentation, cellulite, and other dermatologic contexts, but interventions, routes, combinations, and evidence quality varied substantially.
waves.safety: Route and combination effects are mixed; this review cannot support a general oral L-carnitine skin-health claim.

waves.title: Early-life high-dose omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid supplementation reduces risk of childhood asthma/wheezing: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.population: 4,156 mother-child/early-life participants
waves.finding: Omega-3 supplementation showed no overall reduction in childhood asthma/wheezing; apparent benefit was confined to high-dose subgroup analyses.
waves.safety: Overall null and subgroup-only signal should remain explicit; high-dose prevention strategies are not established.

waves.title: The impact of caffeine consumption on migraine: a systematic review.
waves.study: systematic review of observational and Mendelian-randomization studies
waves.population: large observational/MR datasets plus migraine cohorts
waves.finding: Habitual moderate caffeine exposure was generally not linked to higher migraine burden, while abrupt withdrawal and acute high intake could trigger attacks in susceptible people; genetic-instrument studies suggested lower migraine risk with higher lifelong coffee/caffeine exposure.
waves.safety: Predominantly observational/genetic evidence cannot define a preventive dose; withdrawal and acute excess are clinically relevant trigger contexts.

waves.title: The Effects of Creatine Supplementation on Upper- and Lower-Body Strength and Power: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: 1,937 adults across exercise/training contexts
waves.finding: Creatine, especially with resistance training, produced small significant gains in bench/chest press, squat, vertical jump, and Wingate peak power, while handgrip and overall leg-press effects were not significant.
waves.safety: Subgroup benefits were less consistent in older adults and women; exercise context and endpoint specificity should remain explicit.

waves.title: The effect of turmeric/curcumin supplementation on anthropometric indices in subjects with prediabetes and type 2 diabetes mellitus: A GRADE-assessed systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.population: people with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes
waves.finding: Turmeric/curcumin produced modest reductions in body weight and waist circumference, with some additional anthropometric improvements, but BMI and waist-to-hip ratio were not consistently improved and certainty ranged from very low to moderate.
waves.safety: Small anthropometric changes and nonlinear dose-response analyses do not establish a weight-loss dose or product equivalence.
